players.product: Regulated electric service under the Very Large Customer (VLC) tariff, with new gas, renewable and battery generation and transmission built for Microsoft's data center campus in the I-94 corridor south of Milwaukee and the Vantage Data Centers / Oracle site at Port Washington, Wisconsin

quarterly_data.signal: WEC 10-K: total capital expenditures for the regulated utility businesses are expected to be approximately $33.4 billion from 2026 to 2030, plus approximately $4.1 billion for WEC's share of ATC's projected capital expenditures; estimated capital expenditures are $5,018.1 million in 2026, $6,949.5 million in 2027 and $6,965.6 million in 2028. 2025 capital expenditures were $4,398.1 million versus $2,781.1 million in 2024, the Wisconsin increase driven by renewable energy projects, combustion turbines and an LNG facility at Oak Creek, and electric distribution.
quarterly_data.figure: $33.4 billion utility capex 2026-2030; 2026 capex $5,018.1 million; 2025 capex $4,398.1 million

quarterly_data.signal: WEC 10-K: owned electric generation capacity was 8,375 MW at December 31, 2025 (natural gas 4,193 MW, coal 2,695 MW, solar 773 MW, wind 580 MW); power purchase commitments with unaffiliated parties are 1,133 MW per year for 2026 through 2029, including 1,033 MW per year under the long-term Point Beach nuclear PPA; minimum nuclear purchase commitments total $5,045.8 million through 2033. PSCW-approved jointly owned projects include Koshkonong Solar (270 MW share, expected in service 2026) and High Noon Solar (270 MW, 2027) with 149 MW battery projects at each (2027).
quarterly_data.figure: 8,375 MW owned generation; 1,133 MW per year PPA commitments
